The statement is cautious about near-term growth and inflation due to COVID-19, but it pairs that caution with substantial and credible accommodation: the funds rate held at 0–0.25%, continued Treasury and agency MBS purchases, and explicit average-inflation targeting (a makeup strategy). In line with the literature and the Fed’s own framework, such tools at the zero lower bound—forward guidance and quantitative easing—work by lowering term premia and real rates and by influencing inflation expectations (Federal Reserve utilizes QE and forward guidance; influenced by Cochrane–Piazzesi on yield dynamics; Clarida’s emphasis on the Taylor principle; Powell’s Jackson Hole 2020 shift to AIT; FOMC focus on expectations per Romer and Romer records). This combination mitigates downside risks and supports credit conditions even as the public-health shock weighs on the outlook. Net tone: cautious on activity, clearly supportive on policy.
